Roman River
candidates.extract: The Roman River is a river that flows entirely through the English county of Essex. It is a tributary of the River Colne, flowing into its tidal estuary below Colchester.

candidates.name: UK Data Archive
candidates.extract: The UK Data Archive is a national centre of expertise in data archiving in the United Kingdom. It houses the largest collection of social sciences and population digital data in the UK.

candidates.name: Colchester power station
candidates.description: Former coal-fired power station in England
candidates.extract: Colchester power station supplied electricity to the city of Colchester, Essex, England and the surrounding area from 1900 to 1960. It was owned and operated by Colchester Corporation prior to the nationalisation of the electricity supply industry in 1948.

candidates.name: Rowhedge Ironworks
candidates.extract: Rowhedge Ironworks was a shipyard situated on the River Colne, and in the village of Rowhedge, in the English county of Essex. It existed from 1904 to 1964, and built a number of coastal vessels, including VIC type Clyde puffers and ferries for the Hythe Ferry in Southampton.

candidates.name: The Hythe, Essex
candidates.extract: The Hythe is an area in the southeastern part of Colchester in Essex, England, on the River Colne. Historically it was a hamlet.

Upper Colne Marshes
candidates.extract: Upper Colne Marshes is a 114.1 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south and west of Wivenhoe in Essex. It lies along stretches of the River Colne and Roman River.

candidates.name: Colne Local Nature Reserve
candidates.extract: Colne Local Nature Reserve is a 34.7 hectare Local Nature Reserve in Wivenhoe in Essex. It is owned and managed by Colchester Borough Council.

candidates.extract: Alresford ( or ) is a village and civil parish in the Tendring district of Essex, England. It is centred 9 km southeast of Colchester and is 39 km northeast from the county town of Chelmsford.

Cockaynes Wood
candidates.extract: Cockaynes Wood is a 20.2 hectare nature reserve between Wivenhoe and Alresford in Essex, United Kingdom. It is managed by the Essex Wildlife Trust and the Cockaynes Wood Trust.

candidates.name: Rowhedge
candidates.extract: Rowhedge is a village in the Colchester borough of Essex, England. It is located just over 3 miles south-east of Colchester town centre and is part of the civil parish of East Donyland.

candidates.name: East Donyland
candidates.extract: East Donyland is a civil parish in the City of Colchester district of Essex, England. The main settlement in the parish is the village of Rowhedge.

candidates.name: Alresford railway station (Essex)
candidates.extract: Alresford railway station is on the Sunshine Coast Line, a branch of the Great Eastern Main Line, in the East of England, serving the village of Alresford, Essex. It is 57 mi down the line from London Liverpool Street and is situated between to the west and to the east.

candidates.name: Wivenhoe railway station
candidates.extract: Wivenhoe railway station is on the Sunshine Coast Line, a branch of the Great Eastern Main Line, in the East of England, serving the town of Wivenhoe, Essex. It is 56 mi down the line from London Liverpool Street and is situated between Hythe to the west and Alresford to the east.

Frating Abbey
candidates.extract: Frating Abbey was reputedly an abbey in the village of Frating, in Essex, England. There is no evidence however that there was more than a farm here belonging to either St Botolph's Priory, Colchester, founded c. 1093, or to Wix Priory, founded c. 1125.

candidates.name: Great Bentley
candidates.extract: Great Bentley is a village and civil parish in the Tendring district of north east Essex, England, located seven miles east of Colchester. The village is scattered round an extensive level or common, of 43 acre, on the eastern side of the vale of a rivulet, 7 mi east-south-east of Colchester.

candidates.name: Frating
candidates.extract: Frating is a village and civil parish in the Tendring district of Essex, England. It is about 8 km east of Colchester and 15 km northwest of Clacton-on-Sea.

candidates.name: Great Bentley railway station
candidates.extract: Great Bentley railway station is on the Sunshine Coast Line, a branch of the Great Eastern Main Line, in the East of England, serving the village of Great Bentley as well as the nearby settlements of Brightlingsea, Frating, Thorrington and St Osyth. It is 60 mi down the line from London Liverpool Street and is situated between Alresford to the west and to the east.

candidates.name: Thorington railway station
candidates.extract: Thorington railway station (also Thorrington railway station) was a station in Thorrington, Essex on the line (now called the Sunshine Coast Line) from Colchester to Walton on the Naze and Clacton, opened in 1866 and closed in 1957. The station was situated in between Alresford and Great Bentley.
